title: That Which is Suffering

Yaṁdukkhasutta That Which is Suffering

Sāvatthinidānaṁ. At Sāvatthī.

“Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ. “Mendicants, form is suffering. Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadanattā; What’s suffering is not-self. yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ. And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

Vedanā dukkhā … Feeling is suffering …

saññā dukkhā … Perception is suffering …

saṅkhārā dukkhā … Choices are suffering …

viññāṇaṁ dukkhaṁ. Consciousness is suffering. Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadanattā; What’s suffering is not-self. yadanattā taṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ. And what’s not-self should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

Evaṁ passaṁ …pe… Seeing this … nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

Pañcamaṁ.
